description: Comprehensive guide to identifying and valuing jewelry at estate sales

925.description: 92.5 percent silver, most common sterling mark
925.location: Inside ring band, clasp, or back of pendant

valuable_features: Famous maker marks (Tiffany, Cartier, Van Cleef)

24K.description: Pure gold. Very soft, mostly bullion or coins

22K.description: Common in Middle Eastern and Asian jewelry

18K.description: High quality. Common in European and luxury jewelry

14K.description: Most common US gold jewelry standard

10K.description: Minimum US standard for gold labeling

platinum.value: More valuable than gold by weight. Heavy, dense
platinum.note: Platinum jewelry is very valuable. Look for PT marks.

identification: Look for laser inscription on girdle
diamond.estate_sale_tip: Look for diamond jewelry with certificates. Even small diamonds in silver settings can be valuable.

identification: Deep red color (pigeon blood is most valuable)
ruby.estate_sale_tip: Look for deep red stones in silver or gold settings. Old mine cuts are collectible.

identification: Blue color (can also be pink, yellow, white)
sapphire.estate_sale_tip: Blue stones in silver/gold settings are common. Older cuts (cushion, oval) are collectible.

emerald.estate_sale_tip: Green stones in silver/gold settings. Look for jardin inclusions.

opal.value: Varies widely. Australian black opal most valuable
opal.estate_sale_tip: Look for rainbow flash. Australian opals are most valuable.

pearl.value: Varies widely. Akoya, South Sea, and Tahitian pearls most valuable
identification: Warm to touch (not cold like glass)
Slight toothiness when rubbed against teeth
pearl.estate_sale_tip: Old pearl necklaces are common. Check for matching quality and clasp marks.

garnet.estate_sale_tip: Common but can be valuable in antique Victorian settings.

amber.estate_sale_tip: Look for Baltic amber with fossils. Old carved pieces are collectible.

turquoise.value: Moderate to high. Persian and Sleeping Beauty most valuable
turquoise.estate_sale_tip: Look for Native American silver settings (Navajo, Zuni). Old turquoise in silver is collectible.

Cartier.notable: Tank, Love, Just un Clou, Panthere collections

Tiffany and Co..notable: Elsa Peretti, Paloma Picasso, Return to Tiffany

old_vintage.description: Unmarked antique jewelry can be very valuable

periods.Victorian (1837-1901): Closed back settings, foil backing, cameos
periods.Edwardian (1901-1915): Lace-like filigree, platinum, old European cuts
periods.Art Deco (1920-1935): Geometric designs, onyx, jade, baguette cuts

jewelry_condition_checklist: Check for broken links or solder repairs
Check for hallmarks and maker marks
Check if pieces match (necklaces with earrings, etc.)
jewelry_value_tips: Complete sets (necklace + earrings) worth more than individual pieces
Antique periods (Victorian, Art Deco) command premiums
Gemstones in silver/gold settings are common estate sale finds
Old European cut diamonds are collectible
Natural (not lab-created) stones are more valuable
Jewelry with certificates is worth more
